grammarFocus: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点。
title: The Cost of Convenience: A Town Debates Its Recycling Future
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章是一篇模拟的教育材料，并非官方雅思试题。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（通过单选实现）和判断正误/未提及。填空答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。所有解释均为中文，并附原文证据。
passage:
A. In the small town of Greenfield, residents have been debating whether to keep their current recycling program or switch to a cheaper alternative. The current program, run by the local council, collects paper, glass, and plastic from every household each week. It costs the town about $200,000 per year. However, a private company has offered to provide a similar service for $150,000 annually, but with a catch: residents would need to sort their waste into five categories instead of three, and collection would be every two weeks rather than weekly. The council argues that the savings could be used to improve other public services, such as road repairs and libraries. On the other hand, some residents worry that the change would lead to more confusion and lower recycling rates.

B. At a recent town meeting, opinions were divided. Maria, a mother of two, said, “If we have to sort into five categories, I’m afraid many people will just give up and throw everything in the general waste. That would be worse for the environment.” John, a retired teacher, disagreed. “Although the private company’s plan requires more effort, it saves money. We could use that money to fix the potholes on Main Street, which have been a problem for years.” The council has not yet made a decision. They plan to gather more feedback from residents before the next meeting in June.

C. One alternative that has been suggested is a hybrid approach: keep the weekly collection but reduce the number of categories to two. This would cost $180,000 per year, saving $20,000. However, the private company has said it cannot offer this option because its sorting facility is designed for five categories. The council is also considering a pilot project in one neighborhood to test the five-category system for six months. If the pilot is successful, they might adopt it town-wide. If not, they will stick with the current program. The decision will affect all 15,000 residents of Greenfield.

D. Environmental experts point out that recycling rates in towns with five-category systems are often higher, but only if residents are well informed. Education campaigns can cost money, though. The council has budgeted $10,000 for an awareness campaign if the new system is adopted. Meanwhile, some residents have started a petition against the change, arguing that the current system works well and that the savings are not worth the inconvenience. The petition has collected 2,000 signatures so far. The council will consider the petition at the June meeting.

E. Whatever the outcome, the debate highlights a common dilemma: how to balance cost savings with environmental benefits and public convenience. As Maria put it, “We all want to do the right thing for the planet, but we also need a system that people can actually follow.” The council’s final decision will be watched closely by other towns facing similar choices.

F. The debate has also attracted attention from local businesses. Some shop owners worry that if the town switches to a five-category system, they will have to pay for additional bins and staff training. A local café owner, Susan, said, “We already separate our waste, but five categories would mean more work for my staff. I’m not sure we can afford the extra costs.” On the other hand, a hardware store owner, Mike, sees an opportunity: “If people need more bins, they’ll come to my store. I think the change could be good for business.” The council has promised to consult with local businesses before making any final decision.

G. In addition to the financial and practical concerns, there is also the question of public awareness. A recent survey conducted by the council found that only 40% of residents currently know exactly what can be recycled. This suggests that even the current three-category system is not fully understood. Therefore, some council members argue that before introducing a more complex system, the town should focus on educating residents about the existing rules. Others believe that a new system would force people to learn. The debate continues, and the June meeting is expected to be well attended.

grammar.title: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点
grammar.explanation: 英语中，简单句只有一个主谓结构，而复合句包含两个或多个主谓结构，通过连词连接。条件句常用if引导，表示假设；让步状语从句常用although, though, even though引导，表示转折；原因状语从句常用because, since, as引导。标点方面，复合句中从句和主句之间通常用逗号隔开（如果从句在前）。
grammar.example: Although the private company’s plan requires more effort, it saves money.

options: If it rains, we will stay indoors.
If it rains we will stay indoors.
If it rains; we will stay indoors.
If it rains: we will stay indoors.
answers: If it rains, we will stay indoors.
questions.explanation: 条件状语从句在前时，主句前通常加逗号。

options: Although he was tired, he finished the work.
Although he was tired he finished the work.
Although he was tired; he finished the work.
Although he was tired: he finished the work.
answers: Although he was tired, he finished the work.
questions.explanation: 让步状语从句在前时，主句前加逗号。

options: Because she studied hard, she passed the exam.
Because she studied hard she passed the exam.
Because she studied hard; she passed the exam.
Because she studied hard: she passed the exam.
answers: Because she studied hard, she passed the exam.
questions.explanation: 原因状语从句在前时，主句前加逗号。

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: I like tea, and she likes coffee.
I like tea.
She likes coffee.

answers: I like tea, and she likes coffee.
questions.explanation: 并列句由两个独立分句通过并列连词连接，此处用and连接两个简单句。
